children: Weil Gotshal & Manges' capital markets chief has advised junior lawyers to explore employment opportunities outside the firm amid growing uncertainty about its future, Bloomberg News reported, citing a person familiar with the matter.

Alex Lynch, who heads the New York-based law firm's capital markets practice, delivered the message during a meeting with associates Tuesday, according to Bloomberg News. Although the lawyers will remain employed and continue handling client assignments, Lynch provided no timetable for how long their positions would be secure.

The warning underscores mounting instability at one of Wall Street's prominent legal advisers, raising questions about its ability to retain talent and maintain client relationships. For investors and corporate clients, continued departures could disrupt legal services supporting mergers, securities offerings and financial restructurings, potentially creating opportunities for competing firms.

Weil, which employs more than 1,200 attorneys and generated approximately $2 billion in revenue last year, has experienced a series of departures among senior practice leaders. The losses have fueled concerns about the firm's long-term viability and its ability to preserve key business relationships.

The turmoil follows unsuccessful merger discussions with rival law firm Willkie Farr & Gallagher. Weil subsequently enlisted attorneys from Davis Polk & Wardwell, including restructuring partner Brian Resnick and chairman Neil Barr, as it evaluates its options.
Neither Lynch nor representatives of Weil immediately responded to Bloomberg News's requests for comment.
The developments add to uncertainty surrounding the firm's future, although no formal decision about layoffs, restructuring or a potential combination has been announced.
